why: Both moved the same four chat.completions sites, found and fixed the same two Chat-Completions-only plugin bugs, and left images/audio on OpenAI with the same reasoning — so the migration is effectively a tie, with A's behaviour-equivalence harness and more robust streaming fix against B's larger live sample and its discovery that N_CHOICES/PRESENCE_PENALTY/MAX_TOKENS<16 silently bypass Router entirely. B wins on system-level judgment: its measurements are designed to isolate causes and probe failure modes (cache key with/without and shared-key namespacing, fact-survival before accepting a cheaper summariser, adversarial low-information images that got a vision swap rejected, Flex rejected as wrong for a user-waiting bot), and its review reaches parts of the system A never touches — per-user spend attribution for a bot that has per-user budgets, and the Responses port that would make usage.cost and per-chat keys available.
A_best: Honesty and rigor about what each change costs: every item's "loses" names a real, specific downside (the function_call turn eating a MAX_HISTORY_SIZE slot with measured 58→87 tokens, summary degradation persisting for the rest of the chat, the unguarded Flex tail on buffered calls), plus the sharp app-specific insight that cached input dominates this bot's bill and gpt-5.1's cached-input line is ten times cheaper than gpt-4o's.
B_best: n2 — finding that three ordinary config settings make the runtime forward traffic to OpenAI unnoticed, so a deployment could believe it had migrated while part of its traffic skipped Router and every improvement on it; paired with the cache probe that isolates whether the key causes caching or merely steers it.
A_worst: Headlining i4 as -71% on the Flex tier the account default serves, for a Telegram bot where a human waits and the buffered path has no 25 s fallback guard and a 61 s Flex call was already observed — a savings figure that depends on leaving on the one tier B measured as wrong for this app; and i1's claim that the key only makes caching reliable rather than creating it is contradicted by B's controlled probe.
B_worst: "loses": "nothing" on the cheap-summariser and cross-vendor-fallback items, when both plainly do lose something (a weaker model writes the context the rest of the chat is built on; a different model's voice answers mid-conversation — admitted in the same item's "why"), and deferring provider_timeout to a needs-decision because "someone has to pick the seconds" while a wedged upstream can hold a chat for the SDK's 600 s default.
